title: Maps & Journeys
strapline: Where shall we go, and how will we find our way?
intent: Maps make children's growing sense of place and space visible — from our room, to our garden, to our street.
Following and making maps is real spatial and positional thinking — over, under, past, next to, all the way to.
Journeys connect to children's own lives — the way to nursery, to Grandma's, to the park — and to their local community.
Drawing routes and making maps is purposeful mark-making that carries real meaning.
Treasure hunts and trails turn maps into an irresistible reason to read, follow and give directions.
implementation: Start with the children's own world — draw a map of the room or garden together and use it to find things.
Set up treasure hunts and trails children follow, and then design for each other.
Model positional and direction language: 'Go past the tree, then it's next to the shed.'
Take real journeys — a walk round the block, to the postbox — and map them afterwards.
Provide big paper, clipboards and loose parts so children can draw and build their own maps and routes.
Connect to children's homes and community: where do you live, what do we pass on the way?
Add small-world roads, tracks and journeys so mapping happens in play too.
key_questions: How would we get from here to there — what do we pass?
Can you follow the map to find the treasure?
Where is it hidden — is it next to, under or behind something?
What do we go past on our journey to nursery?
Can you draw a map so your friend can find it too?

impact.text: Children use and understand positional and direction language — over, under, past, next to — as they follow and make maps.
Children talk about journeys, places and their local area, drawing on their own experiences.
Children draw routes and make simple maps, mark-making that carries real meaning.
Children follow a map or trail to find something, reading the marks and symbols for a purpose.
Children give and follow directions to and from each other, holding real back-and-forth talk.
Children notice and talk about features of their community and the wider world.

enhancements: Big paper, clipboards and pens for drawing maps of the room, garden and beyond.
Treasure-hunt cards and trails to follow and to design.
Real, simple maps of the local area, and a globe or world map.
Small-world roads, tracks, rugs and vehicles for mapped journeys in play.
Photos of local landmarks the children know to place on a map.
A compass, torches and 'explorer' kit for outdoor journeys.

playing_exploring: Children explore space and place, following and inventing journeys and hunts.
They test out routes and directions with their own bodies and maps.
active_learning: Children stay with a hunt or a map until they reach the goal.
creating_thinking: Children plan routes, solve how to represent them, and give clear directions to others.
